did_you_know.text: The meaning of “My spirit shall not abide in humans” is not completely clear. The number 120 may refer to a human lifespan or to the time remaining until the Flood.

The word “Nephilim” is probably related to the root meaning “to fall,” but their identity is not clearly explained. Later traditions often described them as giants, while this verse calls them mighty men and famous figures.
In the Bible, “ḥen” means finding favor or goodwill in someone’s eyes. Noah is therefore described as one who found favor with God, even before the text explains his righteousness.
The word “ḥamas” means more than general wickedness; it especially refers to violence, injustice, and harm to others. The verse presents it as a problem that filled the whole society.

“Gopher” is the name of a wood that appears only here in the Bible, so its exact identity is unknown. The “pitch” was a waterproofing material, probably bitumen or something similar, used to keep water out.

The ark’s measurements give it a length-to-width ratio of six to one, making it relatively long and narrow. Since the exact length of a cubit is unknown, its size cannot be calculated precisely in meters.
The word “tsohar” may mean a window, an opening for light, or a source of illumination, so translations differ. The verse also says that the ark had three levels.
